# What is in the box image

<!-- Generated by `go run ./tools/boximage-doc -w` from docker/culibox/Dockerfile. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every boxed session runs in this image (`ghcr.io/culiops/culibox`). This page lists what it ships, at which
version, where each piece comes from and how the build checks it. It is generated from the Dockerfile, and a
test fails when the two drift apart.

## Base image

`node:24-bookworm-slim`, pinned by digest `sha256:a5f4366e834695d5f363b920c104953a535d3a9864d1bdf74566a0ebe01daee5`.
It carries Node.js, npm and the Debian packages of the base itself, which change only when this digest is
bumped.

## Debian packages

Installed with apt from Debian's signed bookworm and bookworm-security archives. The archive is live, not a
snapshot, so each package is at the version Debian served when its image layer was last built. Layers are
cached between builds, so a Debian fix (Chromium's, for one) reaches the image when that layer is rebuilt: a
base digest bump rebuilds every layer.

`bc`, `ca-certificates`, `chromium`, `curl`, `dnsutils`, `file`, `fzf`, `gcc`, `git`, `ipcalc`, `jq`, `less`, `libc6-dev`, `make`, `nano`, `netcat-openbsd`, `openssl`, `procps`, `python3`, `python3-pytest`, `python3-venv`, `ripgrep`, `tree`, `unzip`, `xz-utils`, `zsh`, `zsh-autosuggestions`, `zsh-syntax-highlighting`

## MCP servers the image declares

Declared for every session in `/etc/agent-box/mcp.json`:

| Server |
|---|
| `playwright` |

The other MCP servers in the table above need a URL or a token, so a session declares one only when it binds
a credential for it.

## Services

None. The image runs no daemon: a box runs `sleep infinity` and the processes a session starts.

## Go and the race detector

`gcc` and `libc6-dev` are in the image so the race detector works, and `CGO_ENABLED=0` stays the default so
Go builds stay static, as they were with no compiler. Ask for cgo when you need it:

```
CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -race ./...
```

## Vulnerability scans

- Every image build scans both architectures with a pinned Grype and puts the findings in the box-image
  workflow's job summary.
- A weekly workflow (box-image-scan) scans the `base` image and the one the latest release pins, and keeps
  one issue open, titled "Box image: vulnerabilities with a fix", while a HIGH or CRITICAL finding has a fix.
- Accepted findings are listed in `scripts/ci/image-scan-accepted.txt`, each with a date and a reason, and
  stop counting as accepted 180 days after that date.

Fail policy: report only for now. Once a first baseline has been reviewed, an image build will fail on a
CRITICAL finding that has a fix and is not accepted, and publishing will wait for the scan.
